items.prompt: Do you think money is the most important measure of success?
items.answer: Money matters, but it is not the only measure of success; a person who climbs the career ladder while struggling to make ends meet may be far less content than someone with modest means and a fulfilling life.

items.prompt: Should governments do more to reduce the gap between rich and poor?
items.answer: Yes, I think so; unregulated markets tend to widen the gap between rich and poor, so governments should invest in public services and use fair taxation to support those struggling to make ends meet.

items.prompt: Is it better to work for a company or to be self-employed?
items.answer: It depends on the person; working for a company offers stability, whereas being self-employed offers freedom, so it is really about which side of that trade-off suits you.

blocks.title: Exercise 4.9.3 · Latihan Simulasi Speaking (Simulation Drill)
blocks.instructions: Jawab setiap pertanyaan Part 3 dalam 2–3 kalimat. Gunakan minimal 1 target idiom dan 1 collocation. Lalu bandingkan dengan model answer.

items.prompt: Why is it important to protect traditional culture?
items.answer: Protecting traditional culture matters because it instils a sense of identity and offers a window into the past; customs that stand the test of time connect each generation to the one before it.

items.prompt: Do you think modern life is making traditions disappear?
items.answer: To a certain extent, yes; the fast pace of modern life pushes some customs aside, but renewed interest in heritage means many traditions still stand the test of time.

items.prompt: Should governments spend public money on the arts?
items.answer: I believe they should; public funding sustains the arts, which are an integral part of a nation’s identity and offer a window into its history that the market alone would not preserve.

title: Topic 10 · Media, Komunikasi Massa dan Iklan
blocks: h2
Academic noun (10 kata)
ul
**propaganda** (propaganda): Wartime propaganda shaped public feeling.
**censorship** (sensor): Media censorship limits what citizens can know.
**journalism** (jurnalisme): Independent journalism holds power to account.
**bias** (keberpihakan, bias): Political bias can distort the news.
**consumerism** (konsumerisme): Advertising fuels a culture of consumerism.
**sensationalism** (sensasionalisme, pemberitaan yang dibesar-besarkan): Sensationalism sells papers but misleads readers.
**audience** (penonton, pendengar): Advertisers tailor messages to a target audience.
**misinformation** (informasi yang salah): Misinformation spreads rapidly on social media.
**endorsement** (dukungan, endorsement): A celebrity endorsement can boost sales overnight.
**coverage** (liputan berita): The event received worldwide coverage.
h2
Verb dengan arti yang tepat (10 kata) · bentuk past, participle, -ing
ul
**broadcast** (broadcast, broadcast, broadcasting): The match was broadcast live worldwide.
**manipulate** (manipulated, manipulated, manipulating): Advertisers manipulate our emotions.
**advertise** (advertised, advertised, advertising): Companies advertise heavily during major events.
**influence** (influenced, influenced, influencing): The media strongly influences public opinion.
**endorse** (endorsed, endorsed, endorsing): Athletes endorse products for large fees.
**censor** (censored, censored, censoring): Some governments censor critical reporting.
**exaggerate** (exaggerated, exaggerated, exaggerating): Headlines often exaggerate the facts.
**promote** (promoted, promoted, promoting): Influencers promote brands to their followers.
**distort** (distorted, distorted, distorting): Selective editing can distort a story.
**inform** (informed, informed, informing): A free press informs and educates the public.
h2
Collocation dan adjective (10)
ul
**mass media**: The mass media shapes how we see the world. (Writing)
**freedom of the press**: Freedom of the press is vital to democracy. (Writing)
**target audience**: Every advertisement has a target audience. (Writing)
**misleading advertising**: Misleading advertising should be regulated. (Writing)
**widespread coverage**: The scandal received widespread coverage. (Writing)
**social media**: Social media has changed political campaigning. (Speaking and Writing)
**breaking news**: Breaking news now travels in seconds. (Speaking)
**biased reporting**: Biased reporting undermines public trust. (Writing)
**eye-catching**: An eye-catching advert grabs attention instantly. (Speaking and Writing)
**celebrity endorsement**: Celebrity endorsement drives youth spending. (Writing)
h2
Collocation formal untuk Task 2 (5) · untuk Writing
ul
**shape public opinion**: The media has enormous power to shape public opinion.
**manipulate consumer behaviour**: Clever advertising manipulates consumer behaviour.
**spread misinformation**: Social platforms can spread misinformation at speed.
**play a pivotal role in**: The press plays a pivotal role in a democracy.
**hold those in power to account**: Journalists hold those in power to account.
h2
Idiom dan expression untuk Speaking (5) · hanya dipakai di Speaking
ul
**take it with a pinch of salt**: I take online reviews with a pinch of salt. (Part 3)
**jump on the bandwagon**: Many brands jump on the bandwagon of a trend. (Part 3)
**in the spotlight**: Celebrities are constantly in the spotlight. (Part 2)
**spread like wildfire**: The rumour spread like wildfire. (Part 3)
**hit the headlines**: The story hit the headlines overnight. (Part 3)

blocks.title: Exercise 4.10.1 · Mencocokkan Kata dan Arti (Vocabulary Match)
blocks.instructions:
Cocokkan setiap kata (1 sampai 10) dengan artinya (a sampai j). Ketik hurufnya saja (letter).

a. false or inaccurate information
b. information spread to promote a particular view
c. the suppression of information
d. an unfair leaning toward one side
e. a public statement of support, often for a product
f. a preoccupation with buying goods
g. to control or influence unfairly
h. presenting news to cause maximum excitement
i. to make something seem larger or worse than it is
j. to twist the truth of something

accepted: information spread to promote a particular view
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar b: "information spread to promote a particular view" — artinya informasi yang disebarkan untuk mempromosikan pandangan tertentu.

accepted: the suppression of information
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar c: "the suppression of information" — artinya penekanan atau pembatasan informasi.

accepted: an unfair leaning toward one side
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar d: "an unfair leaning toward one side" — artinya kecenderungan yang tidak adil kepada satu pihak.

accepted: a preoccupation with buying goods
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar f: "a preoccupation with buying goods" — artinya terlalu sibuk memikirkan membeli barang.

accepted: presenting news to cause maximum excitement
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar h: "presenting news to cause maximum excitement" — artinya menyajikan berita agar menimbulkan kehebohan sebesar mungkin.

accepted: false or inaccurate information
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar a: "false or inaccurate information" — artinya informasi yang salah atau tidak akurat.

accepted: a public statement of support, often for a product
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar e: "a public statement of support, often for a product" — artinya pernyataan dukungan secara terbuka, sering untuk suatu produk.

accepted: to control or influence unfairly
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar g: "to control or influence unfairly" — artinya mengendalikan atau memengaruhi secara tidak adil.

accepted: to twist the truth of something
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar j: "to twist the truth of something" — artinya memutarbalikkan kebenaran sesuatu.

accepted: to make something seem larger or worse than it is
items.reason: Jawaban yang benar i: "to make something seem larger or worse than it is" — artinya membuat sesuatu tampak lebih besar atau lebih buruk dari kenyataannya.

blocks.title: Exercise 4.10.3 · Latihan Simulasi Speaking (Simulation Drill)
blocks.instructions: Jawab setiap pertanyaan Part 3 dalam 2–3 kalimat. Gunakan minimal 1 target idiom dan 1 collocation. Lalu bandingkan dengan model answer.

items.prompt: Do you think advertising has too much influence on people?
items.answer: Advertising certainly has too much influence, since clever campaigns manipulate consumer behaviour and encourage people to jump on the bandwagon of every trend, though a discerning viewer learns to take such messages with a pinch of salt.

items.prompt: Can we still trust the news we read online?
items.answer: Not entirely; much online content is biased or sensationalised, and misinformation spreads like wildfire, so it is wise to take what you read with a pinch of salt and check reliable sources.

items.prompt: How has social media changed the way people get information?
items.answer: Social media has transformed how we get information, since breaking news now travels in seconds; the downside is that it also lets rumours spread unchecked.
